**Objectives of the Tutorial/Lab**
By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

- Evaluate bivariate normal densities in R.
- Implement a random-walk Metropolis-Hastings algorithm for bivariate normal distributions.
- Assess acceptance rates and check convergence using Markov chain output.

**Metropolis-Hastings Algorithm**

Recall that $\mathbf{X} = \begin{pmatrix} X_1 \\ X_2 \end{pmatrix} \sim N(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$ with $\boldsymbol{\mu} = \begin{pmatrix} \mu_1 \\ \mu_2 \end{pmatrix}$ and $\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \begin{pmatrix} \sigma_1^2 & \sigma_{12} \\ \sigma_{12} & \sigma_2^2 \end{pmatrix}$, if and only if $\mathbf{X}$ has joint density

$$
f_{\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma}}(\mathbf{x})
=
\frac{1}{2\pi |\boldsymbol{\Sigma}|^{1/2}}
\exp\left\{
-\frac{1}{2}
(\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol{\mu})^T
\boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}
(\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol{\mu})
\right\},
$$

where $\mathbf{x} = \begin{pmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \end{pmatrix}$.
